sections.title: Revenue, Margin & Profitability
sections.subtitle: Three consecutive loss-making years and a multi-year volume trough — FY2026 shows the first clear recovery in trading, obscured at the bottom line by a NZ$51.9m impairment.

charts.title: Revenue & YoY Growth
charts.annotation: FY2026 revenue of $438.9m is +13.9% YoY off the FY2025 trough ($385.4m), but still well below FY2016's $515.9m — eleven years of revenue growth net to roughly zero.

charts.title: EBITDA & EBITDA Margin
charts.annotation: Statutory EBITDA of -$45.8m includes the FY2026 impairment and exit costs. Management's normalised EBITDA (excluding one-offs) was +$9.9m, up from +$2.1m in FY2025 — a genuine operating recovery this chart understates.

charts.title: Net Income
charts.annotation: FY2026's -$61.2m is the largest loss on record, driven by a $51.9m non-cash impairment of business-unit carrying values plus $3.8m of other exit costs tied to leaving reinforcing/wire and plate processing — not a cash operating collapse.

sections.title: Cash Flow & Balance Sheet
sections.subtitle: The going-concern question in three charts: does cash cover the business, has equity been eroded, and how much of the balance sheet is now debt-funded.

charts.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Free Cash Flow
charts.annotation: Reported FCF has stayed positive through the downturn ($5.7m FY2026), but the DCF's owner-FCF adjustment — charging the full NZ$25m of annual lease cash instead of the NZ$18m rent-principal line that sits in financing — turns FY2026 owner FCF negative (-$13.3m). See the DCF section below.

charts.title: Shareholders' Equity & Total Debt
charts.annotation: Equity fell from $182.3m to $121.8m in FY2026 alone, mostly the impairment. Debt rose to $60m (from zero net debt as recently as FY2024) after the debt-funded Perry Metal Protection acquisition, taken on in the depths of a downturn.

charts.title: Shares Outstanding
charts.annotation: 166.0m through FY2023-24 to 183.6m after the FY2025 capital raise (+10.6%) — the last step-change in the count; no buybacks since FY2024.

sections.title: Half-Year Trajectory (H1 FY2022–H1 FY2026)
sections.subtitle: Half-yearly detail shows the deterioration and the recent inflection more precisely than the annual figures alone.

charts.title: H1 Revenue & Net Income
charts.annotation: H1 FY2022 $282.2m revenue / $14.3m profit → H1 FY2025 $196.0m / -$10.4m loss → H1 FY2026 $211.9m / -$12.4m loss. Revenue troughed at H1 FY2025 and is recovering (+8.1% H1 FY2025→H1 FY2026), but the bottom line has not followed because rising net debt now carries a real interest cost through the loss-making trough.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Total sales of steel, stainless, aluminium and metal products and processing/installation services across Distribution and Processing segments.

For Steel & Tube: revenue is a direct read on New Zealand construction and manufacturing volumes — Steel & Tube has essentially no pricing power of its own, so growth here reflects the macro cycle turning, not company-specific execution. FY2026's +13.9% YoY, on +15.9% volumes, is the first clear evidence the multi-year downturn has bottomed, but revenue remains below FY2016 levels eleven years later.

What to watch:

  • Whether the FY2026 volume recovery continues into FY2027, which management has explicitly declined to guide on
  • The revenue mix shift as reinforcing/wire and plate processing are exited during FY27

grossMargin.title: Gross (Product) Margin
grossMargin.content:
Product margin: the spread between input steel cost and selling price, before operating costs.

For Steel & Tube: this is directly exposed to global steel price swings against a ~$114-116m inventory position — falling steel prices produce inventory holding losses that compress the printed margin even when underlying trading is stable. Margin fell from 29.8% (FY2024) to 28.1% (FY2025) partly on pricing pressure, then recovered to 31.1% in 1H FY2026 as steel prices firmed.

What to watch:

  • Whether margin holds above 28% as volumes recover — a re-rate toward FY2022/23 levels (~22% on this chart's GrossMargin definition) is central to the DCF's bull case
  • Steel price direction, which the company does not hedge or disclose granular exposure to

ebitda.title: EBITDA & EBITDA Margin
ebitda.content:
Statutory earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, and that figure as a percentage of revenue.

For Steel & Tube: the statutory FY2026 figure (-$45.8m) is dominated by the $51.9m impairment and exit costs and is not a read on operating performance. Management's own normalised EBITDA — which excludes those one-offs — was +$9.9m in FY2026, up from +$2.1m in FY2025, a genuine ~5x improvement this chart's statutory line obscures. Always cross-check the statutory chart against the normalised figure quoted in results commentary.

What to watch:

  • Whether normalised EBITDA keeps climbing toward the FY2021-23 mid-cycle range (~$40-67m) as volumes recover and the cost-out programmes (~$5m FY24, ~$7m FY25) compound
  • Whether further one-off exit costs appear in FY2027 as the reinforcing/wire and plate businesses are wound down

netIncome.title: Net Income
netIncome.content:
Bottom-line statutory profit or loss after tax.

For Steel & Tube: FY2026's -$61.2m is by far the largest loss in the company's history, driven almost entirely by a $51.9m non-cash impairment of business-unit carrying values (the second major impairment episode after 2018) plus $3.8m of other exit-related costs. It is not primarily a cash event in the year it was booked, but it is a formal admission that a significant amount of shareholder capital deployed into the business has not earned an adequate return.

What to watch:

  • Whether the impairment proves to be a one-off low point or is followed by further write-downs as the reinforcing/wire and plate exits complete
  • Return to sustained profitability, which management has declined to put a date on beyond 'calendar 2027'

fcf.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Free Cash Flow
fcf.content:
Cash generated by operations, and free cash flow (operating cash flow less capital expenditure) as reported under NZ IFRS.

For Steel & Tube: reported FCF has stayed positive even through three loss-making years ($3.6m FY2025, $5.7m FY2026) because IFRS-16 lease principal repayments (~$18m/year) sit in financing activities, not operating cash flow. The DCF valuation adds this back and charges the full ~$25m of annual lease cash (principal + interest) instead, which is why the DCF's 'owner FCF' for FY2026 is -$13.3m — a materially different, and more conservative, number from the reported FCF shown here. Both are shown because they answer different questions: reported FCF is the accounting cash result; owner FCF asks whether the business, including its real occupancy cost, can fund itself.

What to watch:

  • Whether owner FCF (not shown on this chart — see the DCF section) turns positive as EBITDA recovers
  • Working-capital swings around the reinforcing/wire and plate exits, expected to release ~$11-12m of cash by end of FY2027

equityDebt.title: Shareholders' Equity & Total Debt
equityDebt.content:
Total shareholders' equity (net assets) against total interest-bearing debt (bank facilities, excluding IFRS-16 lease liabilities) at each period end.

For Steel & Tube: equity fell from $182.3m to $121.8m in FY2026 alone, almost entirely the impairment. Debt swung from zero net debt as recently as FY2024 to $60m of bank debt ($48m net of cash) after the debt-funded Perry Metal Protection acquisition — taken on in the depths of a downturn and now sitting alongside three consecutive annual losses. The FY2026 audit opinion carries a material uncertainty related to going concern, and ANZ facilities were renegotiated with revised covenants mid-year; the $20m trade loan is repayable on demand and the $40m RCF/term facility expires 4 September 2027.

What to watch:

  • Covenant headroom at future results dates — management's own covenant forecast assumes a market recovery in 2H FY27
  • Progress toward the ~$11-12m of divestment proceeds earmarked for debt reduction

shares.title: Shares Outstanding
shares.content:
Total ordinary shares on issue at each period end.

For Steel & Tube: the share count roughly doubled from 90.6m (pre-Oct-2018) to 166.0m via the 2018/19 covenant-breach recapitalisation, then stepped up again to 183.6m (+10.6%) with the FY2025 capital raise that helped fund the Perry Metal Protection acquisition. No buybacks have occurred since FY2024 (2.896m shares). The DCF models a flat count going forward as a modelling convention (SBC is immaterial at 0.15% of revenue), not a forecast that no further raise will be needed if the downturn extends.

What to watch:

  • Any further capital raise, particularly if covenant pressure returns
  • Whether buybacks resume once net debt is reduced, as management has signalled debt reduction is the current priority ahead of capital return

interim.title: Half-Year Revenue & Net Income
interim.content:
Six-monthly revenue and statutory net income, showing the path through the downturn at finer resolution than the annual figures.

For Steel & Tube: the half-year series shows the trough was H1 FY2025 ($196.0m revenue, -$10.4m loss) and that H1 FY2026 ($211.9m, +8.1% YoY, 54,213t volumes +11.3% YoY) is the first half of clear volume and revenue recovery, even though the loss (-$12.4m) was slightly wider than H1 FY2025's — a sign that rising net debt (now funding real interest cost) and softer product margin timing are still working against the recovering top line at the half-year mark.

What to watch:

  • Whether H2 FY2026's ~40% earnings improvement over H1 (per management commentary) continues into H1 FY2027
  • Management has explicitly declined to give FY2027 guidance, describing the recovery as 'gradual and uneven'

dcf.growth_hint: Base-case Year-1 revenue growth (recovery off the FY2026 trough)
dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — full lease cash charged, SBC expensed
dcf.model_approach_note: This is a mid-cycle earnings-power valuation with an asset cross-check, not a growth DCF, because the FY2026 audit report carries a material-uncertainty-related-to-going-concern paragraph. The model does not extrapolate the FY2026 loss (a trough distorted by a $51.9m non-cash impairment) or the FY2022 windfall (a steel-price inventory gain that reversed); instead it ramps EBITDA margin over four years to roughly FY2024 plus half the benefit of exiting the structurally challenged reinforcing/wire and plate businesses, and capitalises only that. The decisive adjustment is IFRS-16: reported free cash flow looks positive because ~$18m of lease-principal repayment sits in financing, not operating, cash flow. Charging the full ~$25m of lease cash produces mid-cycle owner FCF of roughly $8-10m a year against $48m of net bank debt — at a 14% cost of capital that intrinsic value in the base case is essentially zero, negative in the bear case (flows do not service rent plus debt; a rescue raise would dilute holders to a few cents), and only reaches a positive ~$0.20-0.25/share in a bull case assuming a full decade of FY2022/23-level margins. Book value (NTA ~$0.40/share) is not treated as a floor: the market has paid 0.5-1.0x book for ten years while the price fell 87%, and in a wind-down leases and bank debt absorb most of it — NTA is only reachable via a trade buyer for the network. The honest label for NZ$0.305 against this analysis is a speculative option on a cyclical recovery or a takeout, not a margin-of-safety value buy.
